rule_name: Connection/membership relation can change while participant identity persists
rule_statement: Participant identity does not fix connection/membership state. The canon explicitly permits relation edits such as breaking off, grafting in, grafting back, remaining, and removal; these edits change participation/function while the participant/root/tree identities remain distinguishable.
interpretation_ceiling: This establishes typed connection/membership edits and their consequences. It does not establish a universal graph-edit vocabulary or the full ontology of root/body/community.

rule_name: Member role/function is constrained by placement in a larger relational whole
rule_statement: An isolated member identity is not sufficient to specify its role/function: the canon explicitly nests members in a larger body, assigns placement, differentiates function, and gives mutual member relations. Whole/member placement therefore carries information that is not contained in the member label alone.
condition_signature: member is placed within larger whole
neighbor/body relations and differentiated function are present
consequence_signature: role/function/responsibility depends on whole-member placement relation
interpretation_ceiling: This does not prove that an unknown member's exact state can always be reconstructed from neighbors; it establishes that local identity is relationally constrained by placement in the whole.

rule_name: Persistence of the same governing condition preserves the same operation across duration
rule_statement: When the governing cloud condition remains unchanged, extending its duration from a few days to day/night, two days, a month, or a longer days-period does not change the camp operation: they remain camped and do not set out until the condition changes.
consequence_signature: wait/camp operation remains invariant until cloud lifts
interpretation_ceiling: This is duration-invariance under a persistent condition. It is not proof that repeating an arbitrary operation is generally idempotent.
